fixtures.rule: A body-bearing 2xx response uses a success envelope.
A 4xx response uses fail with one or more issues.
A 5xx response uses error with public-safe issues.
Offset pagination declares its window and self link.
A cursor page with more data includes a cursor and next link.
References and typed links follow their bounded maps.
Every conforming response requires X-Request-Id.
A conforming response uses the selected JsonDispatch vendor media type.
JsonDispatch 3 uses the jd.v3 media-type major.
X-Api-Version-Selected is a full stable semantic version.
HTTP and envelope status classes agree.
A 204 response cannot carry a JsonDispatch envelope.
Unknown top-level envelope members are invalid.
A fail envelope requires an issue array.
A fail or error issue array cannot be empty.
Every issue requires a stable code.
An issue source identifies exactly one location.
Property-map keys are JSON Pointer paths.
A cursor page with has_more=true requires a cursor and next link.
An enriched link object requires href.
Vary identifies both Accept and X-Api-Version.
X-Request-Id is a bounded non-whitespace ASCII token.
Every paginated envelope includes a self link.
Pagination is valid only for array data.
A terminal cursor page does not advertise a next cursor.
Issue codes use uppercase stable machine syntax.
An emitted companion map cannot be empty.
